label: p2: p0's top config (8 epochs) at 400M, seed 6 of 8
notes:
Batch p2 -- eight seeds of batch p0's top config, at 400M transitions.

The config is p0's `p0q-ep8`: eight epochs per rollout instead of four, everything else at the p0
reference (lr 3e-4, gamma 0.99, lambda 0.98, entropy 0.01, fc 320, 128x128 rollout, minibatch 256).
It was 1st of 15 on both metrics -- best30 97.2 and >=98%/500 density 9.7% (21 of 217) -- and its knob
is the only axis p0 found that moved the result: gradient steps per transition, worth 7.5 pp
monotonically (minibatch 1024 at 0.25x scored 89.7, the reference at 1x scored 96.6, this at 2x scored
97.2).

**Why eight seeds.** p0 ran n=1 per config and nine of its fifteen arms finished inside 0.8 pp, which
this project's noise cannot resolve -- CLAUDE.md records the same config producing 62.5 and 18.0. A
single-seed sweep can rank losers and not winners. Seed N is pinned to arm letter N, as everywhere
else in this project, so these are seed-matched against b1a-d, b2a-d, b29a-d, b41a-d and b47a-d.

**Why 400M.** The user's number, and it is a cap rather than a target: 40x p0's budget, to answer
whether a PPO arm keeps improving past 10M. At eight-way contention expect roughly 3,500-4,500
transitions/s per arm on a mature policy, so ~25-32 h per arm -- these will still be running after a
night, which is expected. Read progress off runs/<policy>_evals.json at any point.

**auto_stage_b is OFF for this batch, deliberately.** Stage B over a 400M arm screens ~24,000
checkpoints per arm at >=95, which is days of eval for eight arms. It has to be an explicit decision,
and the wave barrier means an unwanted wave would block everything else on the box.

**The twin batch is on the laptop**: p3a-h, the same eight seeds at the same 400M cap, with p0's other
top config -- fc 200,100, which had the sweep's best single checkpoint (99.2%/500 at 5.05M
transitions) and best30 97.1. Same question, different knob, so the two batches are directly
comparable to each other as well as to p0.
